stories.title: Mawlid cancelled in Tigray
stories.summary: In tonight's programme, the United States on Monday called for beefed-up U.N. sanctions against the warring parties in Sudan. Also, Muslims celebrate Mawlid across Africa but festivities were cancelled in Tigray because of recent drone attacks. And finally in the Kenyan village of Cheporor, a recent discovery of gold sent thousands of amateur prospectors rushing to the area.

stories.title: Biz sentiment rises to near 4-yr high in Aug. on improved service outlook in vacation season: BOK
stories.summary: South Korea's business sentiment rose to a nearly four-year high in August, driven by solid confidence in manufacturing and an improved outlook in the service sector during the summer vacation season, a central bank survey showed Wednesday. The Composite Business Sentiment Index (CBSI) for all industries stood at 99.6 in August, up 1.1 points from the previous month, according to data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The reading marked the highest level since September 2022, when the index recorded 102 after the COVID-19 pandemic. The index measures corporate outlooks on overall business conditions, with a reading below 100 indicating that pessimists outnumber optimists. The BOK said sentiment in the non-manufacturing sector, including transportation and leisure, as well as broadcasting and film, improved during the peak summer vacation season. The CBSI among manufacturers climbed 0.6 point to 103.8 in August from a month earlier, while the index for nonmanufacturing companies added 1.5 points to 96.7. The manufacturing index surpassed the 100 mark for the fourth consecutive month after topping the threshold in May for the first time since August 2022. The outlook for September rose 3.1 points to 99.6 from the previous month's prospect of 96.5, the survey showed. The economic sentiment index, or ESI, which reflects sentiment among both consumers and businesses, went up 1.5 points to 99.4 for August.

stories.title: Corporate direct financing down in July on decreased debt sales
stories.summary: Corporate direct financing fell in July from the previous month due to a fall in bond sales, data showed Wednesday. Local companies raised a combined 26.34 trillion won (US$19.03 billion) last month by selling stocks and bonds, down 0.5 trillion won, or 1.9 percent, from a month earlier, according to the data from the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). Stock sales nearly quadrupled to 1.49 trillion won in July from June, and corporate bond sales fell 1.68 trillion won, or 6.3 percent, to 24.85 trillion won over the cited period. The value of outstanding corporate bonds stood at 766.95 trillion won as of end-July, an increase of 9.72 trillion won, or 1.3 percent, from a month ago, the latest findings showed.
